currentAssumption: Unnamed voters vote in even lean bands around the state's 2024 presidential lean.

recommended.rule: Do not tie ballot-measure vote to presidential lean 1:1. Use topic-specific offsets: abortion-rights and paid sick leave/minimum wage measures ran well ahead of Democratic presidential share in Trump-won states in 2024 (MO, MT, AZ, NE, AK passed). Model measure support = state lean band + topic offset (economic populist measures +10 to +25 points over Democratic lean in Trump states; abortion-rights +5 to +15) with 5-8 point voter-level spread.

unit: percentage points over party lean
basis: NCSL's 2024 review reports abortion-rights measures passed in six states including MO and MT, and minimum wage/sick leave measures passed in NE and MO. Those states went for the Republican presidential nominee, so measure support exceeds party lean. The offset size is a judgment from reported vote shares (Florida abortion measure 57 percent; Missouri wage measure 57-43) and is low confidence.

basis: A study of 143 successful petition drives (via a forum post summarizing it) gives a 75.33 percent mean validity rate. recommended._finding: The EAC's EAVS (2022, 2024) does NOT collect facility type: the 2024 codebook has only counts (D2a-D4c polling places total / not election office / election office, election day and early). Kind shares below are estimates anchored on two measured points (Pennsylvania April 2026 state data: 31% religious, 19% government, 15% schools and libraries, 14% public safety, 12% community/club, 9% commercial/other; Maine 2020: 72 school polling places of about 514 election-day sites) and a national church share of about one in five (Christianity Today, 2022).

CO.note: Vote-center/mail state: few sites (EAVS D3a small); mostly government buildings, libraries, community and college sites.

HI.note: All-mail: EAVS 2024 reports 0 election-day polling places; D4a=13 voter service centers (government buildings, civic centers).

OR.note: Vote-by-mail state: EAVS 2024 D3a=36 election-day sites, D3b (not election offices)=0, i.e. all 36 are county election offices; ballot drop sites are not polling places.

UT.note: Vote-center/mail state: few sites (EAVS D3a small); mostly government buildings, libraries, community and college sites.

WA.note: All-mail: EAVS 2024 reports 0 election-day polling places; D4a=67 voting centers (county election offices, libraries, community buildings).

PR.note: Voting centers (colegios) housed overwhelmingly in public schools (estimate).

unit: percent of polling places by facility kind (per place); EAVS counts in sites
basis: EAVS 2024 V2 (EAC, curl-fetched CSV) gives each state's election-day polling place count (D3a) and early voting sites (D4a) but no facility type, so kinds are not in the EAC data. Two measured anchors (PA 6,572 sites with n=2,018 religious, 1,281 government, 968 school/library, 892 public safety, 830 community/club, 590 other; ME 72 school sites) plus a national church share near 20% set regional archetypes: New England town halls and schools, Mid-Atlantic/Midwest mixed, South church-heavy (AR and OK highest per the same Christianity Today chart), West school/community heavy, and vote-center/mail states (CO, UT, WA, HI, OR) dominated by government buildings. Population-weighted result: church about 21%, schools about 20%. All states except PA, ME and OR are low-confidence estimates (use +/-8 points on each share).

basis: Tax Foundation says seven states newly shifted from graduated to single rate since 2021; four recent conversions with before and after schedules (GA, IA, LA, OH) were fetched and each flat rate was compared with the old schedule average rate on a stylized taxable-income distribution (lognormal, median $42,000, sigma 1.1), giving ratios 0.99, 0.71, 0.82, 0.88. Per-state neutral rates use that same stylized distribution applied to each state 2025 single-filer schedule, ignoring state income differences, so they are low confidence (about +/-1 point); the engine should recompute from its own population. Zero-bracket states (ND, OH, SC) give the rate above their threshold.
